8047 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ obtained spoils, he would order Bilal to call out among the people. They would bring their spoils, and he would take the fifth and divide the rest. Then a man came afterward with a hair rein and said: “O Messenger of Allah, this is from what we obtained from the spoils.” He said: “Did you hear Bilal call out three times?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then what prevented you from bringing it?” He offered an excuse, but he said: “You will be the one to bring it on the Day of Resurrection; I will not accept it from you.”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2712), Ahmad (6996), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4809) and al-Hakim (2/127 and 129).

 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٧١٢)، وأحمد (٦٩٩٦)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٨٠٩)، والحاكم (٢/١٢٧ و١٢٩).
8047 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ obtained spoils, he would order Bilal to call out among the people. They would bring their spoils, and he would take the fifth and divide the rest. Then a man came afterward with a hair rein and said: “O Messenger of Allah, this is from what we obtained from the spoils.” He said: “Did you hear Bilal call out three times?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then what prevented you from bringing it?” He offered an excuse, but he said: “You will be the one to bring it on the Day of Resurrection; I will not accept it from you.”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2712), Ahmad (6996), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4809) and al-Hakim (2/127 and 129).

arabic_source:
٨٠٤٨ — عن عبادة بن الصامت أن النبي ﷺ كان يأخذ الوبرة من جنب البعير من المغنم فيقول: ((ما لي فيه إلا مثل ما لأحدكم منه. إياكم والغلول؛ فإن الغلول خزي على صاحبه يوم القيامة. أدوا الخيط والمخيط وما فوق ذلك، وجاهدوا في سبيل الله تعالى القريب والبعيد، في الحضر والسفر؛ فإن الجهاد باب من أبواب الجنة، إنه لينجي الله تبارك وتعالى به من الهم والغم. وأقيموا حدود الله في القريب والبعيد، ولا يأخذكم في الله لومة لائم)).
 حسن: رواه عبد الله بن أحمد في زوائده على المسند (٢٢٧٩٥).

english_source:
8048 — ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit narrated that the Prophet ﷺ would take a single hair from the side of a camel from the spoils and say: “I have no right in it except like the right of any one of you. Beware of stealing from the spoils, for stealing from the spoils will be disgrace upon its doer on the Day of Resurrection. Return the thread, the needle, and whatever is above that. Strive in the path of Allah Most High, near or far, while resident or traveling, for jihad is one of the gates of Paradise. Through it Allah, Blessed and Most High, saves from anxiety and grief. Establish the limits of Allah for the near and the far, and let not the blame of any blamer affect you regarding Allah.”
 Good: Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn Ahmad in his additions to al-Musnad (22795).

٨٠٤٩ — عن عبد الله بن شقيق أنه أخبره من سمع النبي ﷺ وهو بوادي القرى وهو على فرسه، فسأله رجل من بلقين فقال: يا رسول الله، من هؤلاء؟ قال: ((هؤلاء المغضوب عليهم))، وأشار إلى اليهود. قال: فمن هؤلاء؟ قال: ((هؤلاء الضالون))، يعني النصارى. قال: وجاءه رجل فقال: استشهد مولاك — أو قال: غلامك — فلان. فقال: ((بل يُجر إلى النار في عباءة غلها)).
 صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٠٣٥١).

8049 — ‘Abdullah ibn Shaqiq narrated from one who heard the Prophet ﷺ while he was in Wadi al-Qura, mounted on his horse. A man from Balqayn asked him: “O Messenger of Allah, who are these?” He said: “These are those who incurred wrath,” and he pointed to the Jews. He said: “Then who are these?” He said: “These are those who went astray,” meaning the Christians. He said: A man came to him and said: “Your freedman” — or he said, “your servant” — “so-and-so has been martyred.” He said: “Rather, he is being dragged to the Fire because of a mantle he stole from the spoils.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (20351).

٨٠٥٠ — عن ثابت بن رفيع — وكان يؤمَّر على السرايا — قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((إياكم والغلول: الرجل ينكح المرأة قبل أن تُقسم، ثم يردها إلى القسم، أو يلبس الثوب حتى يخلق، ثم يرده إلى القسم)).
 صحيح: رواه ابن أبي شيبة في مسنده (٦٥٤)، وابن أبي عاصم في الآحاد والمثاني (٢١٩٨)، والطبراني في الكبير (٥/١٦).

8050 — Thabit ibn Rafi‘ — who used to be appointed over detachments — said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Beware of stealing from the spoils: a man has relations with a woman before she is distributed, then returns her to the division; or he wears a garment until it becomes worn out, then returns it to the division.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musnad (654), Ibn Abi ‘Asim in al-Ahad wa al-Mathani (2198), and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (5/16).

٨٠٥١ — عن عبد الله بن عمر: أن رسول الله ﷺ بعث سرية فيها عبد الله بن عمر قبل نجد، فغنموا إبلًا كثيرة، فكان سهمانهم اثني عشر بعيرًا أو أحد عشر بعيرًا، ونُفلوا بعيرًا بعيرًا.
 متفق عليه: رواه مالك (١٠)، والبخاري (٣١٣٤)، ومسلم (١٧٤٩: ٣٥).

8051 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment toward Najd, and ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar was among it. They acquired many camels as spoils. Their shares were twelve camels, or eleven camels, each, and they were each given one camel as an extra share.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (10), al-Bukhari (3134), and Muslim (1749:35).

٨٠٥٢ — عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: نفلنا رسول الله ﷺ نفلًا سوى نصيبنا من الخمس، فأصابني شارف، والشارف: المسن الكبير.

٨٠٥٤ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: نزلت فيَّ أربع آيات. أصبت سيفًا، فأُتي به النبي ﷺ، فقلت: يا رسول الله، نفلنيه. فقال: ((ضعه)). ثم قام، فقال له النبي ﷺ: ((ضعه من حيث أخذته)). ثم قام فقال: نفلنيه يا رسول الله. فقال: ((ضعه)). فقام فقال: يا رسول الله، نفلنيه، أأُجعل كمن لا غناء له؟ فقال له النبي ﷺ: ((ضعه من حيث أخذته)). قال: فنزلت هذه الآية: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَنْفَالِ قُلِ الْأَنْفَالُ لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٧٤٨: ٣٤).

english_source:
8054 — Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas said: Four verses were revealed concerning me. I obtained a sword, and it was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. I said: “O Messenger of Allah, give it to me as an extra share.” He said: “Put it down.” Then he stood up, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Put it where you took it from.” Then he stood and said: “Give it to me as an extra share, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Put it down.” Then he stood and said: “O Messenger of Allah, give it to me as an extra share. Am I to be made like one who has no benefit?” The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Put it where you took it from.” He said: Then this verse was revealed: “They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1748:34).

٨٠٥٥ — عن ابن عباس: أن النبي ﷺ تنفّل سيفه ذا الفقار يوم بدر، وهو الذي رأى فيه الرؤيا يوم أحد.
 حسن: رواه الترمذي (١٥٦١) — واللفظ له — وابن ماجه (٢٨٠٨)، وأحمد (٢٤٤٥)، والحاكم (٢/١٢٨-١٢٩)، وعنه البيهقي في السنن (٧/٤١).

٨٠٥٦ — عن أبي الجويرية قال: أصبت جرة حمراء فيها دنانير في إمارة معاوية بأرض الروم، قال: وعلينا رجل من أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ من بني سليم يقال له: معن بن يزيد. قال: فأتيت بها يقسمها بين المسلمين، فأعطاني مثل ما أعطى رجلًا منهم، ثم قال: لولا أني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ ورأيته يفعله، سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((لا نفل إلا بعد الخمس)) إذًا لأعطيتك. قال: ثم أخذ يعرض علي من نصيبه، فأبيت عليه، قلت: ما أنا بأحق به منك.
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٥٤)، وأحمد (١٥٨٦٢)، والبيهقي (٦/٣١٤). واللفظ لأحمد.

english_source:
8056 — Abu al-Juwayriyah said: I found a red jar containing dinars during the governorship of Mu‘awiyah in the land of the Romans. He said: Over us was a man from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Banu Sulaym called Ma‘n ibn Yazid. He said: I brought it to him so that he could divide it among the Muslims, and he gave me the same as he gave one of them. Then he said: “Were it not that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and saw him do it — I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ‘There is no extra share except after the fifth’ — I would have given you more.” He said: Then he began offering me from his own share, but I refused and said: “I do not have more right to it than you.”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2754), Ahmad (15862), and al-Bayhaqi (6/314). The wording is Ahmad’s.

٨٠٥٧ — عن حبيب بن مسلمة الفهري: كان رسول الله ﷺ ينفّل الثلث بعد الخمس.
 وفي لفظ: أن رسول الله ﷺ نفل الربع بعد الخمس في بدأته، ونفل الثلث بعد الخمس.
 صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٤٨-٢٧٥٠)، وابن ماجه (٢٨٥١)، وأحمد (١٧٤٦٢)، وابن حبان (٤٨٣٥)، والحاكم (٢/١٣٣)، والبيهقي (٦/٣١٤).
 وقوله: “ونفل بعد الخمس” أي أخذ الخمس أولًا من تمام الغنيمة، ثم أعطى الثلث أو الربع مما بقي من الأخماس الأربعة، ثم قسم البقية بين الغانمين.

8057 — Habib ibn Maslamah al-Fihri narrated: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give one-third as an extra share after taking the fifth.
 In another wording: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave one-fourth after taking the fifth at the beginning of the expedition, and one-third after taking the fifth.
 Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2748–2750), Ibn Majah (2851), Ahmad (17462), Ibn Hibban (4835), al-Hakim (2/133), and al-Bayhaqi (6/314).
 His saying, “he gave an extra share after the fifth,” means that he first took the fifth from the entire spoils, then gave one-third or one-fourth from what remained of the four-fifths, then divided the rest among those who had acquired the spoils.
 His saying, “at its beginning,” means at the beginning of the expedition. This refers to a detachment that rises from the army and rushes ahead toward the enemy at the beginning of the campaign; whatever they acquire, he would give them one-fourth of it, and the rest would be divided among the whole army. If a group did something similar when the army was returning, he would give them one-third of what they acquired, because doing that during the return of the army is harder due to the weakness of mounts, equipment, fatigue, and increased longing for home, so he increased it for that reason.

٨٠٥٨ — عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: كانت أموال بني النضير مما أفاء الله على رسوله ﷺ، مما لم يوجف المسلمون عليه بخيل ولا ركاب، فكانت لرسول الله ﷺ خاصة، وكان ينفق على أهله نفقة سنته، ثم يجعل ما بقي في السلاح والكراع عدة في سبيل الله.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٩٠٤)، ومسلم (١٧٥٧: ٤٨).

8058 — ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The wealth of Banu al-Nadir was from what Allah restored to His Messenger ﷺ, for which the Muslims did not spur any horses or camels. It belonged specifically to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He would spend from it on his family for the expenses of a year, then place what remained in weapons and horses as preparation in the path of Allah.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2904) and Muslim (1757:48).

٨٠٥٩ — عن مالك بن أوس بن الحدثان قال: بينا أنا جالس في أهلي حين متع النهار، إذا رسول عمر بن الخطاب يأتيني، فقال: أجب أمير المؤمنين. فانطلقت معه حتى أدخل على عمر، فإذا هو جالس على رمال سرير، ليس بينه وبينه فراش، متكئ على وسادة من أدم. فسلمت عليه، ثم جلست. فقال: يا مال، إنه قدم علينا من قومك أهل أبيات، وقد أمرت فيهم برضخ، فاقبضه فاقسمه بينهم. فقلت: يا أمير المؤمنين، لو أمرت به غيري. قال: اقبضه أيها المرء. فبينا أنا جالس عنده أتاه حاجبه يرفأ، فقال: هل لك في عثمان، وعبد الرحمن بن عوف، والزبير، وسعد بن أبي وقاص، يستأذنون؟ قال: نعم. فأذن لهم، فدخلوا فسلموا وجلسوا. ثم جلس يرفأ يسيرًا، ثم قال: هل لك في علي وعباس؟ قال: نعم. فأذن لهما، فدخلا فسلما فجلسا. فقال عباس: يا أمير المؤمنين، اقض بيني وبين هذا — وهما يختصمان — فيما أفاء الله على رسوله ﷺ من مال بني النضير. فقال الرهط، عثمان وأصحابه: يا أمير المؤمنين، اقض بينهما وأرح أحدهما من الآخر. قال عمر: تيدكم، أنشدكم بالله الذي بإذنه تقوم السماء والأرض، هل تعلمون أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((لا نورث، ما تركنا صدقة)) يريد رسول الله ﷺ نفسه؟ قال الرهط: قد قال ذلك. فأقبل عمر على علي وعباس فقال: أنشدكما بالله، أتعلمان أن رسول الله ﷺ قد قال ذلك؟ قالا: قد قال ذلك. قال عمر: فإني أحدثكم عن هذا الأمر: إن الله قد خص رسوله ﷺ في هذا الفيء بشيء لم يعطه أحدًا غيره، ثم قرأ: (وَمَا أَفَاءَ اللهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ مِنْهُمْ) إلى قوله: (قَدِيرٌ). فكانت هذه خالصة لرسول الله ﷺ. والله ما احتازها دونكم، ولا استأثر بها عليكم، قد أعطاكموها وبثها فيكم، حتى بقي منها هذا المال. فكان رسول الله ﷺ ينفق على أهله نفقة سنتهم من هذا المال، ثم يأخذ ما بقي، فيجعله مجعل مال الله. فعمل رسول الله ﷺ بذلك حياته. أنشدكم بالله، هل تعلمون ذلك؟ قالوا: نعم. ثم قال لعلي وعباس: أنشدكما بالله، هل تعلمان ذلك؟ قالا: نعم. قال عمر: ثم توفى الله نبيه ﷺ، فقال أبو بكر: أنا ولي رسول الله ﷺ. فقبضها أبو بكر، فعمل فيها بما عمل رسول الله ﷺ، والله يعلم إنه فيها لصادق بار راشد تابع للحق. ثم توفى الله أبا بكر، فكنت أنا ولي أبي بكر، فقبضتها سنتين من إمارتي، أعمل فيها بما عمل رسول الله ﷺ وما عمل فيها أبو بكر، والله يعلم إني فيها لصادق بار راشد تابع للحق. ثم جئتماني تكلماني، وكلمتكما واحدة، وأمركما واحد. جئتني يا عباس تسألني نصيبك من ابن أخيك، وجاءني هذا — يريد عليًّا — يريد نصيب امرأته من أبيها. فقلت لكما: إن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((لا نورث، ما تركنا صدقة)). فلما بدا لي أن أدفعه إليكما قلت: إن شئتما دفعتها إليكما على أن عليكما عهد الله وميثاقه لتعملان فيها بما عمل فيها رسول الله ﷺ، وبما عمل فيها أبو بكر، وبما عملت فيها منذ وليتها. فقلتما: ادفعها إلينا. فبذلك دفعتها إليكما. فأنشدكم بالله، هل دفعتها إليهما بذلك؟ قال الرهط: نعم. ثم أقبل على علي وعباس فقال: أنشدكما بالله، هل دفعتها إليكما بذلك؟ قالا: نعم. قال: فتلتمسان مني قضاء غير ذلك؟ فوالله الذي بإذنه تقوم السماء والأرض، لا أقضي فيها قضاء غير ذلك. فإن عجزتما عنها فادفعاها إلي، فإني أكفيكماها.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٠٩٤)، ومسلم (١٧٥٦: ٤٩).

I greeted him, then sat down. He said: “O Malik, some households from your people have come to us, and I have ordered that a gift be given to them. Take it and divide it among them.” I said: “O Commander of the Believers, if only you would order someone else to do it.” He said: “Take it, O man.” While I was sitting with him, his doorkeeper Yarfa’ came and said: “Do you permit ‘Uthman, ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, al-Zubayr, and Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas to enter?” He said: “Yes.” So he gave them permission, and they entered, greeted, and sat. Then Yarfa’ sat a little while and said: “Do you permit ‘Ali and ‘Abbas to enter?” He said: “Yes.” He gave them permission, and they entered, greeted, and sat. Al-‘Abbas said: “O Commander of the Believers, judge between me and this one” — while they were disputing — “concerning what Allah restored to His Messenger ﷺ from the wealth of Banu al-Nadir.” The group, ‘Uthman and his companions, said: “O Commander of the Believers, judge between them and relieve one of them from the other.” ‘Umar said: “Wait. I ask you by Allah, by whose permission the heaven and earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity,’ meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself?” The group said: “He did say that.” Then ‘Umar turned to ‘Ali and ‘Abbas and said: “I ask you both by Allah: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that?” They said: “He did say that.” ‘Umar said: “I will tell you about this matter. Allah singled out His Messenger ﷺ with this fay’ in a way He did not give to anyone else.” Then he recited: “And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them…” until His saying: “Powerful.” “So this belonged exclusively to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Allah, he did not keep it away from you, nor did he prefer himself over you with it. He gave it to you and distributed it among you until this wealth remained from it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to spend from this wealth on his family for their yearly expenses, then take what remained and place it where the wealth of Allah was placed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted according to that during his life. I ask you by Allah: do you know that?” They said: “Yes.” Then he said to ‘Ali and ‘Abbas: “I ask you both by Allah: do you know that?” They said: “Yes.” ‘Umar said: “Then Allah took His Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Bakr said: ‘I am the successor responsible for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.’ Abu Bakr took charge of it and acted with it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had acted. Allah knows that he was truthful, dutiful, rightly guided, and following the truth concerning it. Then Allah took Abu Bakr, and I became the successor responsible after Abu Bakr. I took charge of it for two years of my rule, acting with it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted and as Abu Bakr acted. Allah knows that I was truthful, dutiful, rightly guided, and following the truth concerning it. Then you both came to me speaking to me, and your word was one and your matter was one. You came to me, O ‘Abbas, asking for your share from your nephew, and this one” — meaning ‘Ali — “came to me seeking the share of his wife from her father. I said to you both: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.’ When I decided to hand it over to you both, I said: If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the covenant and pledge of Allah upon you that you will act concerning it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted, as Abu Bakr acted, and as I have acted since I became responsible for it. You both said: ‘Hand it over to us.’ So on that basis I handed it over to you both. I ask you by Allah: did I hand it over to them on that basis?” The group said: “Yes.” Then he turned to ‘Ali and ‘Abbas and said: “I ask you both by Allah: did I hand it over to you on that basis?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “So are you seeking from me a judgment other than that? By Allah, by whose permission the heaven and earth stand, I will not judge concerning it with any judgment other than that. If you are unable to manage it, then hand it back to me, and I will take care of it for you.”

فكان رسول الله ﷺ ينفق على أهله نفقة سنتهم من هذا المال، ثم يأخذ ما بقي، فيجعله مجعل مال الله. فعمل رسول الله ﷺ بذلك حياته. أنشدكم بالله، هل تعلمون ذلك؟ قالوا: نعم. ثم قال لعلي وعباس: أنشدكما بالله، هل تعلمان ذلك؟ قالا: نعم. قال عمر: ثم توفى الله نبيه ﷺ، فقال أبو بكر: أنا ولي رسول الله ﷺ. فقبضها أبو بكر، فعمل فيها بما عمل رسول الله ﷺ، والله يعلم إنه فيها لصادق بار راشد تابع للحق. ثم توفى الله أبا بكر، فكنت أنا ولي أبي بكر، فقبضتها سنتين من إمارتي، أعمل فيها بما عمل رسول الله ﷺ وما عمل فيها أبو بكر، والله يعلم إني فيها لصادق بار راشد تابع للحق. ثم جئتماني تكلماني، وكلمتكما واحدة، وأمركما واحد. جئتني يا عباس تسألني نصيبك من ابن أخيك، وجاءني هذا — يريد عليًّا — يريد نصيب امرأته من أبيها. فقلت لكما: إن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((لا نورث، ما تركنا صدقة)). فلما بدا لي أن أدفعه إليكما قلت: إن شئتما دفعتها إليكما على أن عليكما عهد الله وميثاقه لتعملان فيها بما عمل فيها رسول الله ﷺ، وبما عمل فيها أبو بكر، وبما عملت فيها منذ وليتها. فقلتما: ادفعها إلينا. فبذلك دفعتها إليكما. فأنشدكم بالله، هل دفعتها إليهما بذلك؟ قال الرهط: نعم. ثم أقبل على علي وعباس فقال: أنشدكما بالله، هل دفعتها إليكما بذلك؟ قالا: نعم. قال: فتلتمسان مني قضاء غير ذلك؟ فوالله الذي بإذنه تقوم السماء والأرض، لا أقضي فيها قضاء غير ذلك. فإن عجزتما عنها فادفعاها إلي، فإني أكفيكماها.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٠٩٤)، ومسلم (١٧٥٦: ٤٩).
8059 — Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan said: While I was sitting with my family in the late morning, a messenger of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came to me and said: “Answer the Commander of the Believers.” I went with him until I entered upon ‘Umar, and there he was sitting on the woven matting of a bed, with no mattress between him and it, leaning on a leather cushion. I greeted him, then sat down. He said: “O Malik, some households from your people have come to us, and I have ordered that a gift be given to them. Take it and divide it among them.” I said: “O Commander of the Believers, if only you would order someone else to do it.” He said: “Take it, O man.” While I was sitting with him, his doorkeeper Yarfa’ came and said: “Do you permit ‘Uthman, ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, al-Zubayr, and Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas to enter?” He said: “Yes.” So he gave them permission, and they entered, greeted, and sat. Then Yarfa’ sat a little while and said: “Do you permit ‘Ali and ‘Abbas to enter?” He said: “Yes.” He gave them permission, and they entered, greeted, and sat. Al-‘Abbas said: “O Commander of the Believers, judge between me and this one” — while they were disputing — “concerning what Allah restored to His Messenger ﷺ from the wealth of Banu al-Nadir.” The group, ‘Uthman and his companions, said: “O Commander of the Believers, judge between them and relieve one of them from the other.” ‘Umar said: “Wait. I ask you by Allah, by whose permission the heaven and earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity,’ meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself?” The group said: “He did say that.” Then ‘Umar turned to ‘Ali and ‘Abbas and said: “I ask you both by Allah: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that?” They said: “He did say that.” ‘Umar said: “I will tell you about this matter. Allah singled out His Messenger ﷺ with this fay’ in a way He did not give to anyone else.” Then he recited: “And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them…” until His saying: “Powerful.” “So this belonged exclusively to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Allah, he did not keep it away from you, nor did he prefer himself over you with it. He gave it to you and distributed it among you until this wealth remained from it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to spend from this wealth on his family for their yearly expenses, then take what remained and place it where the wealth of Allah was placed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted according to that during his life. I ask you by Allah: do you know that?” They said: “Yes.” Then he said to ‘Ali and ‘Abbas: “I ask you both by Allah: do you know that?” They said: “Yes.” ‘Umar said: “Then Allah took His Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Bakr said: ‘I am the successor responsible for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.’ Abu Bakr took charge of it and acted with it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had acted. Allah knows that he was truthful, dutiful, rightly guided, and following the truth concerning it. Then Allah took Abu Bakr, and I became the successor responsible after Abu Bakr. I took charge of it for two years of my rule, acting with it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted and as Abu Bakr acted. Allah knows that I was truthful, dutiful, rightly guided, and following the truth concerning it. Then you both came to me speaking to me, and your word was one and your matter was one. You came to me, O ‘Abbas, asking for your share from your nephew, and this one” — meaning ‘Ali — “came to me seeking the share of his wife from her father. I said to you both: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.’ When I decided to hand it over to you both, I said: If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the covenant and pledge of Allah upon you that you will act concerning it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted, as Abu Bakr acted, and as I have acted since I became responsible for it. You both said: ‘Hand it over to us.’ So on that basis I handed it over to you both. I ask you by Allah: did I hand it over to them on that basis?” The group said: “Yes.” Then he turned to ‘Ali and ‘Abbas and said: “I ask you both by Allah: did I hand it over to you on that basis?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “So are you seeking from me a judgment other than that? By Allah, by whose permission the heaven and earth stand, I will not judge concerning it with any judgment other than that. If you are unable to manage it, then hand it back to me, and I will take care of it for you.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3094) and Muslim (1756:49).

٨٠٦٠ — عن عائشة: أن فاطمة ابنة رسول الله ﷺ سألت أبا بكر الصديق بعد وفاة رسول الله ﷺ أن يقسم لها ميراثها مما ترك رسول الله ﷺ مما أفاء الله عليه، فقال لها أبو بكر: إن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((لا نورث، ما تركنا صدقة)). فغضبت فاطمة بنت رسول الله ﷺ، فهجرت أبا بكر، فلم تزل مهاجرته حتى توفيت، وعاشت بعد رسول الله ﷺ ستة أشهر. قالت: وكانت فاطمة تسأل أبا بكر نصيبها مما ترك رسول الله ﷺ من خيبر وفدك وصدقته بالمدينة، فأبى أبو بكر عليها ذلك، وقال: لست تاركًا شيئًا كان رسول الله ﷺ يعمل به إلا عملت به، فإني أخشى إن تركت شيئًا من أمره أن أزيغ. فأما صدقته بالمدينة فدفعها عمر إلى علي وعباس، وأما خيبر وفدك فأمسكهما عمر وقال: هما صدقة رسول الله ﷺ، كانتا لحقوقه التي تعروه ونوائبه، وأمرهما إلى من ولي الأمر. قال: فهما على ذلك إلى اليوم.
 وفي لفظ: أن فاطمة عليها السلام أرسلت إلى أبي بكر تسأله ميراثها من النبي ﷺ فيما أفاء الله على رسوله ﷺ، تطلب صدقة النبي ﷺ التي بالمدينة وفدك وما بقي من خمس خيبر. فقال أبو بكر: إن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((لا نورث، ما تركنا فهو صدقة)). إنما يأكل آل محمد من هذا المال — يعني مال الله — ليس لهم أن يزيدوا على المأكل. وإني والله لا أغير شيئًا من صدقات النبي ﷺ التي كانت عليها في عهد النبي ﷺ، ولأعملن فيها بما عمل فيها رسول الله ﷺ.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٠٩٢-٣٠٩٣)، ومسلم (١٧٥٩: ٥٤).
 ورواه البخاري (٣٧١١-٣٧١٢) باللفظ الثاني.

8060 — ‘A’ishah narrated that Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, asked Abu Bakr al-Siddiq after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to divide for her her inheritance from what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left from what Allah had restored to him. Abu Bakr said to her: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.” Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, became upset with Abu Bakr and stopped speaking to him, and she continued not speaking to him until she died. She lived six months after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: Fatimah used to ask Abu Bakr for her share of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left from Khaybar, Fadak, and his charity in Medina. Abu Bakr refused that to her and said: “I will not leave anything that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do except that I will do it, for I fear that if I leave anything from his command, I would deviate.” As for his charity in Medina, ‘Umar handed it over to ‘Ali and ‘Abbas. As for Khaybar and Fadak, ‘Umar kept them and said: “They are the charity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They were for his rights that would arise and his needs, and their matter belongs to whoever holds authority.” He said: They remain upon that until today.
 In another wording: Fatimah, peace be upon her, sent to Abu Bakr asking him for her inheritance from the Prophet ﷺ regarding what Allah had restored to His Messenger ﷺ. She sought the Prophet’s ﷺ charity in Medina, Fadak, and what remained of the fifth of Khaybar. Abu Bakr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.” The family of Muhammad only eats from this wealth — meaning Allah’s wealth — and they have no right to increase beyond food. “By Allah, I will not change anything from the charities of the Prophet ﷺ as they were during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and I will surely act concerning them as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3092–3093) and Muslim (1759:54).
 Al-Bukhari also narrated it (3711–3712) with the second wording.

Abu Bakr said to her: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.” Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, became upset with Abu Bakr and stopped speaking to him, and she continued not speaking to him until she died. She lived six months after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: Fatimah used to ask Abu Bakr for her share of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left from Khaybar, Fadak, and his charity in Medina. Abu Bakr refused that to her and said: “I will not leave anything that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do except that I will do it, for I fear that if I leave anything from his command, I would deviate.” As for his charity in Medina, ‘Umar handed it over to ‘Ali and ‘Abbas. As for Khaybar and Fadak, ‘Umar kept them and said: “They are the charity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They were for his rights that would arise and his needs, and their matter belongs to whoever holds authority.” He said: They remain upon that until today.
 In another wording: Fatimah, peace be upon her, sent to Abu Bakr asking him for her inheritance from the Prophet ﷺ regarding what Allah had restored to His Messenger ﷺ. She sought the Prophet’s ﷺ charity in Medina, Fadak, and what remained of the fifth of Khaybar. Abu Bakr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.” The family of Muhammad only eats from this wealth — meaning Allah’s wealth — and they have no right to increase beyond food. “By Allah, I will not change anything from the charities of the Prophet ﷺ as they were during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and I will surely act concerning them as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3092–3093) and Muslim (1759:54).
 Al-Bukhari also narrated it (3711–3712) with the second wording.

٨٠٦١ — عن زيد بن أسلم عن أبيه: أن معاوية لما قدم المدينة حاجًّا جاءه عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما، فقال له معاوية: حاجتك يا أبا عبد الرحمن؟ فقال له: حاجتي عطاء المحررين؛ فإني رأيت رسول الله ﷺ أول ما جاءه شيء بدأ بالمحررين.
 حسن: رواه ابن الجارود (١١١٤)، والطحاوي في شرح المشكل (٤٢٧٤)، والبيهقي (٦/٣٤٩).
 قال الخطابي في معالم السنن (٤/٢٠٤): “يريد بالمحررين المعتقين، وذلك أنهم قوم لا ديوان لهم، وإنما يدخلون تبعًا في جملة مواليهم. وكان الديوان موضوعًا على تقديم بني هاشم، ثم الذين يلونهم في القرابة والسابقة، وكان هؤلاء مؤخرين في الذكر، فذكّر بهم عبد الله بن عمر، وتشفع في تقديم أعطيتهم لما علم من ضعفهم وحاجتهم”.

8061 — Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from his father that when Mu‘awiyah came to Medina for Hajj, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, came to him. Mu‘awiyah said to him: “What do you need, O Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman?” He said: “My need is the stipend of the freedmen, for I saw that when something first came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he began with the freedmen.”
 Good: Narrated by Ibn al-Jarud (1114), al-Tahawi in Sharh al-Mushkil (4274), and al-Bayhaqi (6/349).
 Al-Khattabi said in Ma‘alim al-Sunan (4/204): “By ‘freedmen’ he means emancipated slaves. They were a people who had no register of their own; rather, they were included secondarily under their patrons. The register was arranged by giving precedence to Banu Hashim, then those next to them in kinship and precedence. These freedmen were delayed in mention, so ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar reminded him of them and interceded for their stipends to be given earlier because he knew their weakness and need.”

٨٠٦٢ — عن أنس قال في سياق قصة خيبر: فجمع السبي، فجاء دحية فقال: يا نبي الله، أعطني جارية من السبي. قال: ((اذهب فخذ جارية)). فأخذ صفية بنت حيي، فجاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا نبي الله، أعطيت دحية صفية بنت حيي، سيدة قريظة والنضير، لا تصلح إلا لك. قال: ((ادعوه بها)). فجاء بها، فلما نظر إليها النبي ﷺ قال: ((خذ جارية من السبي غيرها)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٧١)، ومسلم (١٣٦٥: ٨٤).

8062 — Anas said, within the story of Khaybar: The captives were gathered, and Dihyah came and said: “O Prophet of Allah, give me a slave-woman from the captives.” He said: “Go and take a slave-woman.” So he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Prophet of Allah, you have given Dihyah Safiyyah bint Huyayy, the lady of Qurayzah and al-Nadir; she is suitable only for you.” He said: “Call him with her.” He brought her, and when the Prophet ﷺ looked at her, he said: “Take another slave-woman from the captives.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (371) and Muslim (1365:84).

٨٠٦٤ — عن مالك بن أوس بن الحدثان قال: كان فيما احتج به عمر أنه قال: كانت لرسول الله ﷺ ثلاث صفايا: بنو النضير، وخيبر، وفدك. فأما بنو النضير فكانت حبسًا لنوائبه، وأما فدك فكانت حبسًا لأبناء السبيل، وأما خيبر فجزأها رسول الله ﷺ ثلاثة أجزاء: جزءين بين المسلمين، وجزءًا نفقة لأهله، فما فضل عن نفقة أهله جعله بين فقراء المهاجرين.
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٩٦٧)، والبزار (٢٥٦)، والبيهقي (٦/٢٩٦).

8064 — Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan said: Among the arguments presented by ‘Umar was that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had three chosen properties: Banu al-Nadir, Khaybar, and Fadak. As for Banu al-Nadir, it was reserved for his unexpected needs. As for Fadak, it was reserved for travelers. As for Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided it into three parts: two parts among the Muslims, and one part for the expenses of his family. Whatever remained beyond the expenses of his family, he placed among the poor of the Muhajirun.
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2967), al-Bazzar (256), and al-Bayhaqi (6/296).

٨٠٦٤ — عن مالك بن أوس بن الحدثان قال: كان فيما احتج به عمر أنه قال: كانت لرسول الله ﷺ ثلاث صفايا: بنو النضير، وخيبر، وفدك. فأما بنو النضير فكانت حبسًا لنوائبه، وأما فدك فكانت حبسًا لأبناء السبيل، وأما خيبر فجزأها رسول الله ﷺ ثلاثة أجزاء: جزءين بين المسلمين، وجزءًا نفقة لأهله، فما فضل عن نفقة أهله جعله بين فقراء المهاجرين.
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٩٦٧)، والبزار (٢٥٦)، والبيهقي (٦/٢٩٦).
8064 — Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan said: Among the arguments presented by ‘Umar was that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had three chosen properties: Banu al-Nadir, Khaybar, and Fadak. As for Banu al-Nadir, it was reserved for his unexpected needs. As for Fadak, it was reserved for travelers. As for Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided it into three parts: two parts among the Muslims, and one part for the expenses of his family. Whatever remained beyond the expenses of his family, he placed among the poor of the Muhajirun.
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2967), al-Bazzar (256), and al-Bayhaqi (6/296).

٨٠٦٦ — عن يزيد بن عبد الله قال: كنا بالمربد، إذ جاء رجل أشعث الرأس بيده قطعة أديم أحمر، فقلنا: كأنك من أهل البادية؟ فقال: أجل. قلنا: ناولنا هذه القطعة الأديم التي في يدك. فناولناها، فقرأناها، فإذا فيها:
 من محمد رسول الله إلى بني زهير بن أقيش: إنكم إن شهدتم أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدًا رسول الله، وأقمتم الصلاة، وآتيتم الزكاة، وأديتم الخمس من المغنم، وسهم النبي ﷺ، وسهم الصفي، أنتم آمنون بأمان الله ورسوله. فقلنا: من كتب لك هذا الكتاب؟ قال: رسول الله ﷺ.
 صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٩٩٩)، وأحمد (٢٠٧٤٠)، وصححه ابن حبان (٦٥٥٧).

8066 — Yazid ibn ‘Abdullah said: We were at al-Mirbad when a man with disheveled hair came, holding a piece of red leather in his hand. We said: “You seem to be from the desert people?” He said: “Yes.” We said: “Hand us this piece of leather that is in your hand.” He handed it to us, and we read it. It contained:
 “From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Banu Zuhayr ibn Uqaysh: If you testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish prayer, give zakah, and pay the fifth from the spoils, the share of the Prophet ﷺ, and the chosen share, then you are safe under the protection of Allah and His Messenger.” We said: “Who wrote this document for you?” He said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2999), Ahmad (20740), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (6557).

٨٠٦٧ — عن ابن عباس قال: قدم وفد عبد القيس فقالوا: يا رسول الله، إنا هذا الحي من ربيعة، بيننا وبينك كفار مضر، فلسنا نصل إليك إلا في الشهر الحرام، فمرنا بأمر نأخذ به وندعو إليه من وراءنا. قال: ((آمركم بأربع وأنهاكم عن أربع: الإيمان بالله: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله)) — وعقد بيده — ((وإقام الصلاة، وإيتاء الزكاة، وصيام رمضان، وأن تؤدوا خمس ما غنمتم. وأنهاكم عن الدباء، والنقير، والحنتم، والمزفت)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٠٩٥)، ومسلم (١٧: ٢٣).

8067 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays came and said: “O Messenger of Allah, we are this tribe from Rabi‘ah, and between us and you are the disbelievers of Mudar, so we can only reach you during the sacred month. Command us with something we may hold to and call those behind us to.” He said: “I command you with four and forbid you from four: faith in Allah — testifying that there is no god but Allah” — and he counted it with his hand — “establishing prayer, giving zakah, fasting Ramadan, and giving the fifth of what you acquire as spoils. And I forbid you from al-dubba’, al-naqir, al-hantam, and al-muzaffat.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3095) and Muslim (17:23).

 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1756).

٨٠٦٩ — عن عمرو بن عبسة قال: صلى بنا رسول الله ﷺ إلى بعير من المغنم، فلما سلم أخذ وبرة من جنب البعير، ثم قال: ((ولا يحل لي من غنائمكم مثل هذا إلا الخمس، والخمس مردود فيكم)).
 صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٥٥)، ومن طريقه البيهقي (٦/٣٣٩).

When he gave salām, he took a single hair from the side of the camel, then said: “Not even the like of this from your spoils is lawful for me except the fifth, and the fifth is returned among you.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2755), and through him by al-Bayhaqi (6/339).

 صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٥٥)، ومن طريقه البيهقي (٦/٣٣٩).
8069 — ‘Amr ibn ‘Abasah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer facing a camel from the spoils. When he gave salām, he took a single hair from the side of the camel, then said: “Not even the like of this from your spoils is lawful for me except the fifth, and the fifth is returned among you.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2755), and through him by al-Bayhaqi (6/339).

arabic_source:
٨٠٧٠ — عن عبادة بن الصامت قال: أخذ رسول الله ﷺ يوم حنين وبرة من جنب بعير، فقال: ((يا أيها الناس، إنه لا يحل لي مما أفاء الله عليكم قدر هذه إلا الخمس، والخمس مردود عليكم)).
 حسن: رواه النسائي (٤١٣٨)، وأحمد (٢٢٧١٨)، والبيهقي (٦/٣٠٣).

٨٠٧١ — عن جبير بن مطعم أخبره قال: مشيت أنا وعثمان بن عفان إلى النبي ﷺ، فقلنا: أعطيت بني المطلب من خمس خيبر وتركتنا، ونحن بمنزلة واحدة منك. فقال: ((إنما بنو هاشم وبنو المطلب شيء واحد)).
 قال جبير: ولم يقسم النبي ﷺ لبني عبد شمس وبني نوفل شيئًا.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٢٢٩). ورواه أبو داود (٢٩٧٨) وزاد: قال: وكان أبو بكر يقسم الخمس نحو قسم رسول الله ﷺ، غير أنه لم يكن يعطي قربى رسول الله ﷺ ما كان النبي ﷺ يعطيهم. قال: وكان عمر بن الخطاب يعطيهم منه، وعثمان بعده.

8071 — Jubayr ibn Mut‘im reported: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan and I walked to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “You gave Banu al-Muttalib from the fifth of Khaybar and left us, though we and they are in the same position in relation to you.” He said: “Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib are only one thing.”
 Jubayr said: The Prophet ﷺ did not give anything to Banu ‘Abd Shams or Banu Nawfal.
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (4229). Abu Dawud (2978) also narrated it and added: Abu Bakr used to divide the fifth in a manner similar to the division of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, except that he did not give the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what the Prophet ﷺ had given them. He said: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab used to give them from it, and ‘Uthman after him.

٨٠٧٢ — عن جبير بن مطعم قال: لما كان يوم خيبر وضع رسول الله ﷺ سهم ذي القربى في بني هاشم وبني المطلب، وترك بني نوفل وبني عبد شمس. فانطلقت أنا وعثمان بن عفان حتى أتينا النبي ﷺ، فقلنا: يا رسول الله، هؤلاء بنو هاشم لا ننكر فضلهم للموضع الذي وضعك الله به منهم، فما بال إخواننا بني المطلب أعطيتهم وتركتنا، وقرابتنا واحدة؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إنا وبنو المطلب لا نفترق في جاهلية ولا إسلام، وإنما نحن وهم شيء واحد))، وشبك بين أصابعه.
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٩٨٠)، والنسائي (٤١٣٧)، وأحمد (١٦٧٤١)، والبيهقي (٦/٣٤١).

8072 — Jubayr ibn Mut‘im said: On the day of Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed the share of near relatives among Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, and left Banu Nawfal and Banu ‘Abd Shams. So I and ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan went until we came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, as for Banu Hashim, we do not deny their virtue due to the position in which Allah placed you among them. But what about our brothers Banu al-Muttalib? You gave them and left us, though our kinship is the same.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We and Banu al-Muttalib did not separate in the pre-Islamic period or in Islam; rather, we and they are one thing,” and he interlaced his fingers.
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2980), al-Nasa’i (4137), Ahmad (16741), and al-Bayhaqi (6/341).

٨٠٧٣ — عن يزيد بن هرمز: أن نجدة الحروري حين خرج في فتنة ابن الزبير أرسل إلى ابن عباس يسأله عن سهم ذي القربى: لمن تراه؟ قال: هو لنا، لقربى رسول الله ﷺ، قسمه رسول الله ﷺ لهم. وقد كان عمر عرض علينا شيئًا رأيناه دون حقنا، فأبينا أن نقبله. وكان الذي عرض عليهم: أن يعين ناكحهم، ويقضي عن غارمهم، ويعطي فقيرهم، وأبى أن يزيدهم على ذلك.
 صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٩٨٢)، والنسائي (٤١٣٣)، وأحمد (٢٩٤١). والسياق للنسائي وأحمد.

8073 — Yazid ibn Hurmuz narrated that when Najdah al-Haruri rebelled during the turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr, he sent to Ibn ‘Abbas asking him about the share of near relatives: “For whom do you consider it?” He said: “It is for us, due to our kinship with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided it for them. ‘Umar had offered us something that we considered less than our right, so we refused to accept it.” What he offered them was that he would help the one among them who wished to marry, pay the debt of their debtor, and give to their poor; but he refused to give them more than that.
 Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2982), al-Nasa’i (4133), and Ahmad (2941). The wording is that of al-Nasa’i and Ahmad.

8074 — Nashirah ibn Sumayy al-Yazani said: I heard ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, speaking on the day of al-Jabiyah while addressing the people: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made me the treasurer of this wealth and its distributor.” Then he said: “Rather, Allah distributes it, and I will begin with the family of the Prophet ﷺ, then with the noblest among them.” He assigned ten thousand to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, except Juwayriyah, Safiyyah, and Maymunah. ‘A’ishah said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to be just among us,” so ‘Umar made them equal.
 Then he said: “I will begin with my companions, the earliest Muhajirun, for we were expelled from our homes unjustly and aggressively, then the noblest among them.” He assigned five thousand to those among them who attended Badr, four thousand to those from the Ansar who attended Badr, and three thousand to those who attended Uhud. He said: “Whoever was early in migration will be given early in stipend, and whoever was late in migration will be delayed in stipend. So let no man blame anyone but the resting place of his mount. And I apologize to you regarding Khalid ibn al-Walid. I ordered him to reserve this wealth for the weak among the Muhajirun, but he gave it to people of strength, status, and eloquence, so I removed him and appointed Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah.” Abu ‘Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah said: “By Allah, you have not excused yourself, O ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab. You removed a governor whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had appointed, sheathed a sword that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had drawn, lowered a banner that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had raised, severed kinship, and envied your cousin.” ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said: “You are close in kinship, young in age, and angry on behalf of your cousin.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (15905).

8075 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, no one is wounded in the path of Allah — and Allah knows best who is wounded in His path — except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound flowing with blood: its color will be the color of blood, but its fragrance will be the fragrance of musk.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (29), al-Bukhari (2803), and Muslim (1876:105).

8076 — Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, were it not that some men among the believers would not feel content to remain behind from me, and I do not find mounts to carry them on, I would not remain behind from any detachment that goes forth in the path of Allah. By the One in whose hand is my soul, I wish that I could be killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, then killed, then brought back to life, then killed, then brought back to life, then killed.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2797) and Muslim (1876).

٨٠٧٦ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: ((والذي نفسي بيده، لولا أن رجالًا من المؤمنين لا تطيب أنفسهم أن يتخلفوا عني، ولا أجد ما أحملهم عليه، ما تخلفت عن سرية تغزو في سبيل الله. والذي نفسي بيده، لوددت أني أقتل في سبيل الله، ثم أحيا ثم أقتل، ثم أحيا ثم أقتل، ثم أحيا ثم أقتل)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٧٩٧)، ومسلم (١٨٧٦).

٨٠٧٧ — عن أنس بن مالك، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((ما أحد يدخل الجنة يحب أن يرجع إلى الدنيا وله ما على الأرض من شيء إلا الشهيد، يتمنى أن يرجع إلى الدنيا فيقتل عشر مرات؛ لما يرى من الكرامة)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٨١٧)، ومسلم (١٨٧٧: ١٠٩).

8077 — Anas ibn Malik narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “No one who enters Paradise would love to return to the world, even if he had everything on earth, except the martyr. He wishes to return to the world and be killed ten times because of the honor he sees.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2817) and Muslim (1877:109).

٨٠٧٨ — عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((يؤتى بالرجل من أهل الجنة، فيقول الله عز وجل: يا ابن آدم، كيف وجدت منزلك؟ فيقول: أي رب، خير منزل. فيقول: سل وتمنَّ. فيقول: أسألك أن تردني إلى الدنيا، فأقتل في سبيلك عشر مرات؛ لما يرى من فضل الشهادة)).
 صحيح: رواه النسائي (٣١٦٠)، وأحمد (١٢٣٤٢)، والحاكم (٢/٧٥).

8078 — Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A man from the people of Paradise will be brought, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: ‘O son of Adam, how did you find your dwelling?’ He will say: ‘My Lord, the best dwelling.’ He will say: ‘Ask and wish.’ He will say: ‘I ask You to return me to the world so that I may be killed in Your path ten times,’ because of what he sees of the virtue of martyrdom.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (3160), Ahmad (12342), and al-Hakim (2/75).

٨٠٧٩ — عن ابن أبي عميرة: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((ما من الناس من نفس مسلمة يقبضها ربها تحب أن ترجع إليكم وأن لها الدنيا وما فيها غير الشهيد)).
 قال ابن أبي عميرة: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((لأن أقتل في سبيل الله أحب إلي من أن يكون لي أهل الوبر والمدر)).
 حسن: رواه النسائي (٣١٥٣)، وأحمد (١٧٨٩٤).

8079 — Ibn Abi ‘Umayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no Muslim soul among the people whose Lord takes it that would love to return to you, even if it had the world and everything in it, except the martyr.”
 Ibn Abi ‘Umayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “To be killed in the path of Allah is more beloved to me than to possess the people of tents and towns.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (3153) and Ahmad (17894).

٨٠٨٠ — عن عبادة بن الصامت أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((ما على الأرض من نفس تموت ولها عند الله خير، تحب أن ترجع إليكم ولها الدنيا، إلا القتيل، فإنه يحب أن يرجع فيقتل مرة أخرى)).
 حسن: رواه النسائي (٣١٥٩)، والطبراني في الأوسط (٤٠١).

8080 — ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no soul on earth that dies and has good with Allah, which would love to return to you even if it had the world, except the one killed in Allah’s path. He loves to return and be killed again.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (3159) and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (401).

٨٠٨١ — عن سمرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ: ((رأيت الليلة رجلين أتياني، فصعدا بي الشجرة، فأدخلاني دارًا هي أحسن وأفضل، لم أر قط أحسن منها. قالا: أما هذه الدار فدار الشهداء)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٧٩١).

8081 — Samurah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Tonight I saw two men who came to me. They took me up a tree and entered me into a house that was the most beautiful and excellent; I had never seen anything more beautiful than it. They said: As for this house, it is the house of the martyrs.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2791).

٨٠٨٢ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((يضحك الله إلى رجلين يقتل أحدهما الآخر، كلاهما يدخل الجنة: يقاتل هذا في سبيل الله فيقتل، ثم يتوب الله على القاتل فيقاتل فيستشهد)).
 متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٢٨)، والبخاري (٢٨٢٦)، ومسلم (١٨٩٠: ١٢٨).

8082 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah laughs at two men, one of whom kills the other, and both enter Paradise: this one fights in the path of Allah and is killed; then Allah accepts the repentance of the killer, so he fights and is martyred.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (28), al-Bukhari (2826), and Muslim (1890:128).

٨٠٨٣ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((ما يجد الشهيد من مس القتل إلا كما يجد أحدكم من مس القرصة)).
 حسن: رواه الترمذي (١٦٦٨) وصححه، والنسائي (٣١٦١)، وابن ماجه (٢٨٠٢)، وأحمد (٧٩٥٣)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٦٥٥).
 وقوله: “القرصة” بفتح القاف وسكون الراء، من القرص. قال في القاموس: القرص أخذك لحم إنسان بأصبعيك حتى تؤلمه، ولسع البراغيث.

8083 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The martyr does not feel the touch of being killed except as one of you feels the touch of a pinch.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1668), who authenticated it, al-Nasa’i (3161), Ibn Majah (2802), Ahmad (7953), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4655).
 “Al-qarṣah,” with an open qaf and a silent ra’, comes from “pinching.” It says in al-Qamus: “al-qarṣ” is when you take a person’s flesh between two fingers until you hurt him, and it also refers to flea bites.

8084 — Abu Umamah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “There is nothing more beloved to Allah than two drops and two traces: a drop of tears out of fear of Allah, and a drop of blood shed in the path of Allah. As for the two traces: a trace in the path of Allah, and a trace in one of the obligations of Allah.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1669), who graded it good, and Ibn Abi ‘Asim in al-Jihad (108).

٨٠٨٥ — عن معاذ بن جبل أنه سمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((من قاتل في سبيل الله عز وجل من رجل مسلم فواق ناقة وجبت له الجنة، ومن سأل الله القتل من عند نفسه صادقًا، ثم مات أو قتل، فله أجر شهيد. ومن جرح جرحًا في سبيل الله أو نكب نكبة، فإنها تجيء يوم القيامة كأغزر ما كانت، لونها كالزعفران، وريحها كالمسك. ومن جرح جرحًا في سبيل الله، فعليه طابع الشهداء)).
 حسن: رواه النسائي (٣١٤١)، والبيهقي (٩/١٧٠)، والترمذي (١٦٥٤، ١٦٥٧) مفرقًا، وأحمد (٢٢١١٦)، والحاكم (٢/٧٧) مختصرًا، وابن ماجه (٢٧٩٢) مختصرًا، وأحمد (٢٢٠١٤، ٢٢١١٦)، وعبد الرزاق في المصنف (٩٥٣٤).

8085 — Mu‘adh ibn Jabal heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Any Muslim man who fights in the path of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the time between two milkings of a she-camel, Paradise becomes obligatory for him. Whoever sincerely asks Allah for being killed, then dies or is killed, will have the reward of a martyr. Whoever is wounded in the path of Allah or suffers an injury, it will come on the Day of Resurrection as abundant as it ever was, its color like saffron and its fragrance like musk. Whoever is wounded in the path of Allah will bear the mark of the martyrs.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (3141), al-Bayhaqi (9/170), al-Tirmidhi (1654, 1657) in separate portions, Ahmad (22116), al-Hakim (2/77) in abridged form, Ibn Majah (2792) in abridged form, Ahmad (22014, 22116), and ‘Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (9534).

8086 — Al-Miqdam ibn Ma‘dikarib narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: “The martyr has six qualities with Allah: he is forgiven at the first flow of his blood; he sees his seat in Paradise; he is protected from the punishment of the grave; he is safe from the greatest terror; he is adorned with the garment of faith; he is married to the wide-eyed maidens; and he intercedes for seventy people from his relatives.”
 Good: Narrated by Ibn Majah (2799).

٨٠٨٧ — عن قيس الجذامي — رجل كانت له صحبة — قال: قال النبي ﷺ: ((يعطى الشهيد ست خصال: عند أول قطرة من دمه يكفّر عنه كل خطيئة، ويرى مقعده من الجنة، ويزوج من الحور العين، ويؤمن من الفزع الأكبر، ومن عذاب القبر، ويحلّى حلة الإيمان)).
 حسن: رواه أحمد (١٧٨٨٣).

english_source:
8087 — Qays al-Judhami — a man who had companionship — said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The martyr is given six qualities: at the first drop of his blood, every sin is expiated from him; he sees his seat in Paradise; he is married to the wide-eyed maidens; he is protected from the greatest terror and from the punishment of the grave; and he is adorned with the garment of faith.”
 Good: Narrated by Ahmad (17883).

arabic_source:
٨٠٨٨ — عن رجل من أصحاب النبي ﷺ أن رجلًا قال: يا رسول الله، ما بال المؤمنين يفتنون في قبورهم إلا الشهيد؟ قال: ((كفى ببارقة السيوف على رأسه فتنة)).
 صحيح: رواه النسائي (٢٠٥٣).

english_source:
8088 — A man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ narrated that a man said: “O Messenger of Allah, why are the believers tested in their graves except the martyr?” He said: “The flashing of swords over his head is enough of a trial for him.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (2053).

٨٠٨٩ — عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((الشهداء على بارق نهر بباب الجنة، في قبة خضراء، يخرج عليهم رزقهم من الجنة بكرة وعشيًّا)).
 حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٩٠)، وابن أبي عاصم في الجهاد (١٩٩)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٦٥٨)، والحاكم (٢/٧٤).

8089 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The martyrs are on the bank of a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome. Their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening.”
 Good: Narrated by Ahmad (2390), Ibn Abi ‘Asim in al-Jihad (199), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4658) and al-Hakim (2/74).

٨٠٩٠ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((أفضل الجهاد عند الله يوم القيامة الذين يلتقون في الصف، فلا يلفتون وجوههم حتى يقتلوا، أولئك يتلبطون في الغرف العلى من الجنة، ينظر إليهم ربك، إن ربك إذا ضحك إلى قوم فلا حساب عليهم)).
 حسن: رواه الطبراني في الأوسط (٢٦٨٤ — مجمع البحرين).

8090 — Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best fighters in Allah’s sight on the Day of Resurrection are those who meet in the battle-line and do not turn their faces until they are killed. They will move about in the highest chambers of Paradise. Your Lord looks at them, and when your Lord laughs toward a people, there is no reckoning upon them.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (2684 — Majma‘ al-Bahrayn).

٨٠٩١ — عن نعيم بن همّار أن رجلًا سأل النبي ﷺ: أي الشهداء أفضل؟ قال: ((الذين إن يُلقَوا في الصف لا يلفتون وجوههم حتى يُقتلوا، أولئك يتلبطون في الغرف العلى من الجنة، ويضحك إليهم ربك، وإذا ضحك ربك إلى عبد في الدنيا فلا حساب عليه)).
 حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٢٤٧٦)، وأبو يعلى (٦٨٥٥)، وابن أبي عاصم في الجهاد (٢٢٨)، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (٩٨٦)، والآجري في الشريعة (٦٥٠).

8091 — Nu‘aym ibn Hammar narrated that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ: “Which martyrs are best?” He said: “Those who, when they are placed in the battle-line, do not turn their faces until they are killed. They will move about in the highest chambers of Paradise, and your Lord laughs toward them. When your Lord laughs toward a servant in this world, there is no reckoning upon him.”
 Good: Narrated by Imam Ahmad (22476), Abu Ya‘la (6855), Ibn Abi ‘Asim in al-Jihad (228), al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa al-Sifat (986), and al-Ajurri in al-Shari‘ah (650).

٨٠٩٢ — عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((يُشفّع الشهيد في سبعين من أهل بيته)).
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٥٢٢). ثم قال أبو داود: صوابه: «رباح بن الوليد».

8092 — Abu al-Darda’ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The martyr will be allowed to intercede for seventy of his family.”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2522). Abu Dawud then said: “The correct form is Rabah ibn al-Walid.”

٨٠٩٣ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رجل للنبي ﷺ يوم أحد: أرأيت إن قتلت فأين أنا؟ قال: ((في الجنة)). فألقى تمرات في يده ثم قاتل حتى قتل.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٠٤٦)، ومسلم (١٨٩٩: ١٤٣).

8093 — Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah said: On the day of Uhud, a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Tell me, if I am killed, where will I be?” He said: “In Paradise.” So he threw away some dates that were in his hand, then fought until he was killed.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (4046) and Muslim (1899:143).

 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٠٤٦)، ومسلم (١٨٩٩: ١٤٣).
8093 — Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah said: On the day of Uhud, a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Tell me, if I am killed, where will I be?” He said: “In Paradise.” So he threw away some dates that were in his hand, then fought until he was killed.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (4046) and Muslim (1899:143).

٨٠٩٤ — عن أنس قال: عمي الذي سميت به لم يشهد مع رسول الله ﷺ بدرًا. قال: فشق عليه، قال: أول مشهد شهده رسول الله ﷺ غبت عنه، وإن أراني الله مشهدًا فيما بعد مع رسول الله ﷺ ليرين الله ما أصنع. قال: فهاب أن يقول غيرها. قال: فشهد مع رسول الله ﷺ يوم أحد. قال: فاستقبل سعد بن معاذ، فقال له أنس: يا أبا عمرو، أين؟ فقال: واها لريح الجنة، أجده دون أحد. قال: فقاتلهم حتى قتل. قال: فوجد في جسده بضع وثمانون ما بين ضربة وطعنة ورمية. قال: فقالت أخته عمتي الربيع بنت النضر: فما عرفت أخي إلا ببنانه. ونزلت هذه الآية: (رِجَالٌ صَدَقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا اللهَ عَلَيْهِ فَمِنْهُم مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَنتَظِرُ وَمَا بَدَّلُوا تَبْدِيلًا) [الأحزاب: ٢٣]. قال: فكانوا يرون أنها نزلت فيه وفي أصحابه.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٨٠٥)، ومسلم (١٩٠٣: ١٤٨). واللفظ لمسلم.

8094 — Anas said: My uncle, after whom I was named, did not attend Badr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: That was hard for him. He said: “The first battle witnessed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I was absent from it. If Allah shows me a battle afterward with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah will surely see what I will do.” He said: He was hesitant to say more than that. He then witnessed Uhud with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He met Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh, and Anas said to him: “O Abu ‘Amr, where are you going?” He said: “Ah, the fragrance of Paradise! I find it before Uhud.” He fought them until he was killed. More than eighty wounds were found on his body, between sword-strikes, spear-thrusts, and arrow-wounds. His sister, my aunt al-Rubayyi‘ bint al-Nadr, said: “I only recognized my brother by his fingertips.” Then this verse was revealed: “Among the believers are men who were true to what they pledged to Allah. Among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who are waiting, and they have not changed in the least.” [al-Ahzab: 23] He said: They used to think that it was revealed concerning him and his companions.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2805) and Muslim (1903:148). The wording is Muslim’s.

٨٠٩٥ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: جاء ناس إلى النبي ﷺ فقالوا: أن ابعث معنا رجالًا يعلمونا القرآن والسنة. فبعث إليهم سبعين رجلًا من الأنصار يقال لهم القراء، فيهم خالي حرام. يقرؤون القرآن، ويتدارسون بالليل يتعلمون، وكانوا بالنهار يجيئون بالماء فيضعونه في المسجد، ويحتطبون فيبيعونه، ويشترون به الطعام لأهل الصفة وللفقراء. فبعثهم النبي ﷺ إليهم، فعرضوا لهم، فقتلوهم قبل أن يبلغوا المكان. فقالوا: اللهم بلغ عنا نبينا أنا قد لقيناك فرضينا عنك ورضيت عنا. قال: وأتى رجل حرامًا، خال أنس، من خلفه، فطعنه برمح حتى أنفذه. فقال حرام: فزت ورب الكعبة. فقال رسول الله ﷺ لأصحابه: ((إن إخوانكم قد قتلوا، وإنهم قالوا: اللهم بلغ عنا نبينا أنا قد لقيناك فرضينا عنك ورضيت عنا)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (٦٧٧: ١٤٧)، والبخاري (٢٨٠١).

8095 — Anas ibn Malik said: Some people came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Send with us men who will teach us the Qur’an and the Sunnah.” So he sent to them seventy men from the Ansar who were called the Qurra’, among whom was my maternal uncle Haram. They used to recite the Qur’an and study together at night, learning, and during the day they would bring water and place it in the mosque, gather firewood and sell it, and buy food with it for the people of al-Suffah and the poor. The Prophet ﷺ sent them to those people, but they attacked them and killed them before they reached the place. They said: “O Allah, convey from us to our Prophet that we have met You, and we are pleased with You, and You are pleased with us.” He said: A man came to Haram, the maternal uncle of Anas, from behind and pierced him with a spear until it went through him. Haram said: “I have succeeded, by the Lord of the Ka‘bah.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: “Your brothers have been killed, and they said: O Allah, convey from us to our Prophet that we have met You, and we are pleased with You, and You are pleased with us.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (677:147) and al-Bukhari (2801).

8096 — Ka‘b ibn Malik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The souls of the martyrs are in green birds, eating from the fruit of Paradise or the trees of Paradise.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1641) and Ahmad (27166). He said: “This is a good authentic hadith.”

٨٠٩٦ — عن كعب بن مالك، أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((إن أرواح الشهداء في طير خضر، تعلق من ثمرة الجنة أو شجر الجنة)).
 صحيح: رواه الترمذي (١٦٤١)، وأحمد (٢٧١٦٦). وقال: “هذا حديث حسن صحيح”.

٨٠٩٧ — عن مسروق قال: سألنا عبد الله بن مسعود عن هذه الآية: (وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ أَمْوَاتًا بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ). قال: أما إنا قد سألنا عن ذلك، فقال: ((أرواحهم في جوف طير خضر، لها قناديل معلقة بالعرش، تسرح من الجنة حيث شاءت، ثم تأوي إلى تلك القناديل. فاطلع إليهم ربهم اطلاعة، فقال: هل تشتهون شيئًا؟ قالوا: أي شيء نشتهي، ونحن نسرح من الجنة حيث شئنا؟ ففعل ذلك بهم ثلاث مرات، فلما رأوا أنهم لن يتركوا من أن يسألوا قالوا: يا رب، نريد أن ترد أرواحنا في أجسادنا حتى نقتل في سبيلك مرة أخرى. فلما رأى أن ليس لهم حاجة تركوا)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٨٧: ١٢١).

8097 — Masruq said: We asked ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud about this verse: “Do not think of those who were killed in the path of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” He said: We did ask about that, and he said: “Their souls are inside green birds. They have lamps hanging from the Throne. They roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, then return to those lamps. Their Lord looks upon them and says: ‘Do you desire anything?’ They say: ‘What could we desire while we roam freely in Paradise wherever we wish?’ He does that with them three times. When they see that they will not be left without being asked, they say: ‘Our Lord, we want You to return our souls to our bodies so that we may be killed in Your path once more.’ When He sees that they have no need, He leaves them.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1887:121).

٨٠٩٨ — عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((لما أصيب إخوانكم بأحد، جعل الله أرواحهم في جوف طير خضر، ترد أنهار الجنة، تأكل من ثمارها، وتأوي إلى قناديل من ذهب معلقة في ظل العرش. فلما وجدوا طيب مأكلهم ومشربهم ومقيلهم، قالوا: من يبلغ إخواننا عنا أنا أحياء في الجنة نرزق، لئلا يزهدوا في الجهاد ولا ينكلوا عند الحرب؟ فقال الله سبحانه: أنا أبلغهم عنكم. قال: فأنزل الله: (وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ) إلى آخر الآية)).
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٥٢٠).

8098 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When your brothers were struck down at Uhud, Allah placed their souls inside green birds that come to the rivers of Paradise, eat from its fruits, and return to lamps of gold hanging in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their food, drink, and resting place, they said: ‘Who will convey to our brothers from us that we are alive in Paradise, receiving provision, so that they will not turn away from jihad or shrink back during war?’ Allah, Glorified is He, said: ‘I will convey it from you.’ He said: Then Allah revealed: ‘Do not think of those who were killed in the path of Allah…’ to the end of the verse.”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2520).

٨٠٩٩ — عن أبي قتادة أنه سمعه يحدث عن رسول الله ﷺ أنه قام فيهم فذكر لهم: أن الجهاد في سبيل الله والإيمان بالله أفضل الأعمال. فقام رجل فقال: يا رسول الله، أرأيت إن قتلت في سبيل الله تكفر عني خطاياي؟ فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: ((نعم، إن قتلت في سبيل الله وأنت صابر محتسب، مقبل غير مدبر)). ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((كيف قلت؟)) قال: أرأيت إن قتلت في سبيل الله أتكفر عني خطاياي؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((نعم، وأنت صابر محتسب، مقبل غير مدبر، إلا الدين؛ فإن جبريل عليه السلام قال لي ذلك)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٨٥: ١١٧).

8099 — Abu Qatadah narrated that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing among them and mentioning to them that jihad in the path of Allah and faith in Allah are the best deeds. A man stood and said: “O Messenger of Allah, tell me, if I am killed in the path of Allah, will my sins be expiated from me?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Yes, if you are killed in the path of Allah while patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How did you put it?” He said: “Tell me, if I am killed in the path of Allah, will my sins be expiated from me?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Yes, while you are patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating — except debt, for Jibril, peace be upon him, said that to me.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1885:117).

A man stood and said: “O Messenger of Allah, tell me, if I am killed in the path of Allah, will my sins be expiated from me?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Yes, if you are killed in the path of Allah while patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How did you put it?” He said: “Tell me, if I am killed in the path of Allah, will my sins be expiated from me?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Yes, while you are patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating — except debt, for Jibril, peace be upon him, said that to me.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1885:117).

٨١٠٢ — عن سهل بن حنيف قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((أول ما يهراق من دم الشهيد يغفر له ذنبه كله إلا الدين)).
 حسن: رواه أبو يعلى (١٩٢٦ — المطالب)، والطبراني في الكبير (٦/٨٨)، والحاكم (٢/١١٩)، وعنه البيهقي (٩/١٦٣-١٦٤). وليس عند الحاكم والبيهقي: «إلا الدين».

٨١٠٤ — عن محمد بن عبد الله بن جحش قال: كنا جلوسًا بفناء المسجد حيث توضع الجنائز، ورسول الله ﷺ جالس بين ظهرانينا، فرفع رسول الله ﷺ بصره قبل السماء، فنظر، ثم طأطأ بصره، ووضع يده على جبهته، ثم قال: ((سبحان الله، سبحان الله، ماذا نزل من التشديد؟)) قال: فسكتنا يومنا وليلتنا، فلم نرها خيرًا حتى أصبحنا. قال محمد: فسألت رسول الله ﷺ: ما التشديد الذي نزل؟ قال: ((في الدين. والذي نفس محمد بيده، لو أن رجلًا قتل في سبيل الله، ثم عاش، ثم قتل في سبيل الله، ثم عاش، ثم قتل في سبيل الله، ثم عاش، وعليه دين، ما دخل الجنة حتى يقضي دينه)).
 حسن: رواه النسائي (٤٦٨٤)، وأحمد (٢٢٤٩٣)، والحاكم (٢/٢٥).

8104 — Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh said: We were sitting in the courtyard of the mosque where the funerals were placed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting among us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his gaze toward the sky and looked, then lowered his gaze, placed his hand on his forehead, and said: “Glory be to Allah, glory be to Allah! What severity has been revealed?” He said: We remained silent that day and night, and we did not see it as good until morning came. Muhammad said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “What severity was revealed?” He said: “Concerning debt. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if a man were killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, then killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, then killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, while he had a debt upon him, he would not enter Paradise until his debt was paid.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (4684), Ahmad (22493), and al-Hakim (2/25).

٨١٠٤ — عن محمد بن عبد الله بن جحش قال: كنا جلوسًا بفناء المسجد حيث توضع الجنائز، ورسول الله ﷺ جالس بين ظهرانينا، فرفع رسول الله ﷺ بصره قبل السماء، فنظر، ثم طأطأ بصره، ووضع يده على جبهته، ثم قال: ((سبحان الله، سبحان الله، ماذا نزل من التشديد؟)) قال: فسكتنا يومنا وليلتنا، فلم نرها خيرًا حتى أصبحنا. قال محمد: فسألت رسول الله ﷺ: ما التشديد الذي نزل؟ قال: ((في الدين. والذي نفس محمد بيده، لو أن رجلًا قتل في سبيل الله، ثم عاش، ثم قتل في سبيل الله، ثم عاش، ثم قتل في سبيل الله، ثم عاش، وعليه دين، ما دخل الجنة حتى يقضي دينه)).
 حسن: رواه النسائي (٤٦٨٤)، وأحمد (٢٢٤٩٣)، والحاكم (٢/٢٥).
8104 — Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh said: We were sitting in the courtyard of the mosque where the funerals were placed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting among us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his gaze toward the sky and looked, then lowered his gaze, placed his hand on his forehead, and said: “Glory be to Allah, glory be to Allah! What severity has been revealed?” He said: We remained silent that day and night, and we did not see it as good until morning came. Muhammad said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “What severity was revealed?” He said: “Concerning debt. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if a man were killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, then killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, then killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, while he had a debt upon him, he would not enter Paradise until his debt was paid.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (4684), Ahmad (22493), and al-Hakim (2/25).

arabic_source:
٨١٠٥ — عن محمد بن عبد الله بن جحش: أن رجلًا جاء إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: ما لي يا رسول الله إن قتلت في سبيل الله؟ قال: ((الجنة)). قال: فلما ولى قال: ((إلا الدين، سارّني به جبريل عليه السلام آنفًا)).
 حسن: رواه أحمد (١٧٢٥٣، ١٩٠٧٧)، وابن أبي شيبة (٣/٢٧٣)، وعنه ابن أبي عاصم في الجهاد (٢/٢٣٨).

 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٩٠٨: ١٥٦).

٨١٠٨ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان النبي ﷺ يجمع بين الرجلين من قتلى أحد في ثوب واحد، ثم يقول: ((أيهم أكثر أخذًا للقرآن؟)) فإذا أشير له إلى أحدهما قدّمه في اللحد، وقال: ((أنا شهيد على هؤلاء يوم القيامة)). وأمر بدفنهم في دمائهم، ولم يُغسلوا، ولم يُصلَّ عليهم.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٣٤٣).

8108 — Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah said: The Prophet ﷺ used to place two men from those killed at Uhud together in one cloth, then say: “Which of them had taken more of the Qur’an?” When one of them was pointed out to him, he would place him first in the grave niche, and he said: “I am a witness over these people on the Day of Resurrection.” He ordered that they be buried in their blood; they were not washed, and the funeral prayer was not performed over them.
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1343).

٨١٠٩ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((بينما رجل يمشي بطريق إذ وجد غصن شوك على الطريق، فأخره، فشكر الله له، فغفر له)). وقال: ((الشهداء خمسة: المطعون، والمبطون، والغرق، وصاحب الهدم، والشهيد في سبيل الله)). ثم ذكر حديث فضل الصف الأول في صلاة الجماعة.
 صحيح: رواه مالك (٦)، والبخاري (٦٥٢-٦٥٤، ٢٨٢٩)، ومسلم (١٩١٤: ١٦٤).

english_source:
8109 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “While a man was walking on a road, he found a thorny branch on the road and removed it. Allah appreciated that from him and forgave him.” He also said: “The martyrs are five: one who dies of plague, one who dies of a stomach illness, one who drowns, one who dies under a collapsed structure, and the martyr in the path of Allah.” Then he mentioned the hadith about the virtue of the first row in congregational prayer.
 Authentic: Narrated by Malik (6), al-Bukhari (652–654, 2829), and Muslim (1914:164).

8110 — Abu Hurayrah said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if a man comes wanting to take my wealth?” He said: “Do not give him your wealth.” He said: “What if he fights me?” He said: “Fight him.” He said: “What if he kills me?” He said: “Then you are a martyr.” He said: “What if I kill him?” He said: “He is in the Fire.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (140).

8110 — Abu Hurayrah said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if a man comes wanting to take my wealth?” He said: “Do not give him your wealth.” He said: “What if he fights me?” He said: “Fight him.” He said: “What if he kills me?” He said: “Then you are a martyr.” He said: “What if I kill him?” He said: “He is in the Fire.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (140).

arabic_source:
٨١١١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((ما تعدون الشهيد فيكم؟)) قالوا: يا رسول الله، من قتل في سبيل الله فهو شهيد. قال: ((إن شهداء أمتي إذا لقليل)). قالوا: فمن هم يا رسول الله؟ قال: ((من قتل في سبيل الله فهو شهيد، ومن مات في سبيل الله فهو شهيد، ومن مات في الطاعون فهو شهيد، ومن مات في البطن فهو شهيد)).
 قال ابن مقسم: أشهد على أبيك في هذا الحديث أنه قال: ((والغريق شهيد)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٩١٥: ١٦٥).

8111 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whom do you count as a martyr among you?” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, whoever is killed in the path of Allah is a martyr.” He said: “Then the martyrs of my ummah would be few.” They said: “Then who are they, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Whoever is killed in the path of Allah is a martyr; whoever dies in the path of Allah is a martyr; whoever dies of plague is a martyr; and whoever dies of a stomach illness is a martyr.”
 Ibn Miqsam said: I testify concerning your father in this hadith that he said: “And the one who drowns is a martyr.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1915:165).

٨١١٢ — عن عائشة قالت: سألت رسول الله ﷺ عن الطاعون، فأخبرني: ((أنه عذاب يبعثه الله على من يشاء، وأن الله جعله رحمة للمؤمنين، ليس من أحد يقع الطاعون، فيمكث في بلده صابرًا محتسبًا، يعلم أنه لا يصيبه إلا ما كتب الله له، إلا كان له مثل أجر شهيد)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٤٧٤).

8112 — ‘A’ishah said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about plague, and he informed me: “It is a punishment that Allah sends upon whom He wills, and Allah has made it a mercy for the believers. There is no one upon whom plague falls, and he remains in his land patiently seeking reward, knowing that nothing will befall him except what Allah has written for him, except that he will have the like of the reward of a martyr.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3474).

٨١١٣ — عن حفصة بنت سيرين قالت: قال لي أنس بن مالك: بم مات يحيى ابن أبي عمرة؟ قالت: قلت: بالطاعون. قالت: فقال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((الطاعون شهادة لكل مسلم)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٨٣٠)، ومسلم (١٩١٦: ١٦٦).

8113 — Hafsah bint Sirin said: Anas ibn Malik said to me: “What did Yahya ibn Abi ‘Amrah die of?” She said: I said: “Of plague.” She said: He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Plague is martyrdom for every Muslim.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2830) and Muslim (1916:166).

 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2480) and Muslim (141).

٨١١٥ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((تُستشهدون بالقتل، والطاعون، والغرق، والبطن، وموت المرأة جمعًا: موتها في نفاسها)).
 صحيح: رواه أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة في مسنده (١٩٢٠ — المطالب)، وعبد بن حميد (١٥٤)، ومن طريقه الضياء في المختارة (٢/٢٢٥)، والبزار (١١٩١).

8115 — Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Martyrdom is attained through being killed, plague, drowning, stomach illness, and a woman dying while pregnant or in childbirth — that is, her death during postpartum bleeding.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musnad (1920 — al-Matalib), ‘Abd ibn Humayd (154), through whom al-Diya’ narrated it in al-Mukhtarah (2/225), and al-Bazzar (1191).

8116 — Sa‘id ibn Zayd said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever is killed defending his wealth is a martyr; whoever is killed defending his religion is a martyr; whoever is killed defending his life is a martyr; and whoever is killed defending his family is a martyr.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1421), whose wording this is, Abu Dawud (4772), al-Nasa’i (4094, 4095), and Ahmad (1652).

 صحيح: رواه الترمذي (١٤٢١) — والسياق له —، وأبو داود (٤٧٧٢)، والنسائي (٤٠٩٤، ٤٠٩٥)، وأحمد (١٦٥٢).
8116 — Sa‘id ibn Zayd said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever is killed defending his wealth is a martyr; whoever is killed defending his religion is a martyr; whoever is killed defending his life is a martyr; and whoever is killed defending his family is a martyr.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1421), whose wording this is, Abu Dawud (4772), al-Nasa’i (4094, 4095), and Ahmad (1652).

 صحيح: رواه ابن أبي عاصم في الجهاد (٢٣٧)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٧/٣٢٣).

٨١١٨ — عن جابر بن عتيك: أن رسول الله ﷺ جاء يعود عبد الله بن ثابت، فوجده قد غُلب عليه، فصاح به فلم يجبه، فاسترجع رسول الله ﷺ وقال: ((غُلبنا عليك يا أبا الربيع)). فصاح النسوة وبكين، فجعل جابر يسكتهن. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((دعهن، فإذا وجب فلا تبكين باكية)). قالوا: يا رسول الله، وما الوجوب؟ قال: ((إذا مات)). فقالت ابنته: والله إن كنت لأرجو أن تكون شهيدًا، فإنك كنت قد قضيت جهازك. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إن الله قد أوقع أجره على قدر نيته، وما تعدون الشهادة؟)) قالوا: القتل في سبيل الله. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((الشهداء سبعة سوى القتل في سبيل الله: المطعون شهيد، والغرق شهيد، وصاحب ذات الجنب شهيد، والمبطون شهيد، والحرق شهيد، والذي يموت تحت الهدم شهيد، والمرأة تموت بجمع شهيد)).
 حسن: رواه مالك في الجنائز (٣٦).
 وقوله: “ذات الجنب” هي ورم حار يعرض في الغشاء المستبطن للأضلاع.
 وقوله: “قد قضيت جهازك” أي قد أعددت ما تحتاج إليه في سفرك للغزو.

english_source:
8118 — Jabir ibn ‘Atik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit ‘Abdullah ibn Thabit and found him overcome by death. He called out to him, but he did not respond. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return,” and said: “We have been overcome concerning you, O Abu al-Rabi‘.” The women cried out and wept, and Jabir began silencing them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Leave them. But when it becomes certain, no woman should weep.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, what is ‘when it becomes certain’?” He said: “When he dies.” His daughter said: “By Allah, I had hoped that you would be a martyr, for you had already prepared your equipment.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah has assigned his reward according to his intention. What do you count as martyrdom?” They said: “Being killed in the path of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The martyrs are seven besides being killed in the path of Allah: the one who dies of plague is a martyr; the one who drowns is a martyr; the one who dies of pleurisy is a martyr; the one who dies of a stomach illness is a martyr; the one who dies by burning is a martyr; the one who dies beneath a collapsed structure is a martyr; and the woman who dies while pregnant or in childbirth is a martyr.”
 Good: Narrated by Malik in al-Jana’iz (36).
 “Dhat al-janb” is a hot swelling that occurs in the membrane lining the ribs.
 His saying, “you had already prepared your equipment,” means: you had prepared what you needed for your journey to battle.

8119 — Rabi‘ al-Ansari narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited the nephew of Jabr al-Ansari. His family began weeping over him, so Jabr said to them: “Do not bother the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Leave them to weep as long as he is alive. But once it becomes certain, they should be silent.” Some of them said: “We did not think that your death would be on your bed; we expected you to be killed in the path of Allah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Is martyrdom only in being killed in the path of Allah? Then the martyrs of my ummah would be few. Stabbing and plague are martyrdom; stomach illness is martyrdom; the postpartum woman dying while her child is still joined to her is martyrdom; burning is martyrdom; drowning is martyrdom; dying under a collapse is martyrdom; and pleurisy is martyrdom.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (5/65).

٨١٢١ — عن العرباض بن سارية قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((يختصم الشهداء والمتوفون على فرشهم إلى الله عز وجل في الذين ماتوا من الطاعون، فيقول الشهداء: إخواننا قتلوا، ويقول المتوفون على فرشهم: إخواننا ماتوا على فرشهم كما متنا. فيقضي الله بينهم: أن انظروا إلى جراحات المطعونين، فإن أشبهت جراحات الشهداء فهم منهم. فينظرون إلى جراح المطعونين، فإذا هي قد أشبهت جراح الشهداء، فيلحقون معهم)).
 حسن: رواه أحمد (١٧١٦٤).

8121 — Al-‘Irbad ibn Sariyah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The martyrs and those who died on their beds will dispute before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, concerning those who died of plague. The martyrs will say: ‘Our brothers were killed.’ Those who died on their beds will say: ‘Our brothers died on their beds just as we died.’ Allah will judge between them: ‘Look at the wounds of those who died of plague. If they resemble the wounds of the martyrs, then they are from them.’ They will look at the wounds of those who died of plague, and behold, they resemble the wounds of the martyrs, so they will be joined with them.”
 Good: Narrated by Ahmad (17164).

٨١٢٢ — عن عبد الله بن بسر المازني قال: عاد رسول الله ﷺ سعد بن عبادة، فقال: ((ما تعدون الشهداء من أمتي؟)) قال: قال ذلك ثلاثًا. قلنا: الله ورسوله أعلم. قال سعد بن عبادة: إن شاء رسول الله ﷺ أذن لي فأخبرته من الشهداء من أمته. قال: ((فأخبرني، من الشهداء من أمتي؟)) قال: أسندوني. فأسندوه، فقال: ((من آمن بالله وجاهد في سبيل الله وقاتل حتى قتل، فهو شهيد)). قال: ((إن شهداء أمتي إذًا لقليل: القتيل في سبيل الله شهيد، والمبطون شهيد، والمطعون شهيد، والغريق شهيد، والنفساء شهيد)).
 حسن: رواه الطبراني في مسند الشاميين (١٥٠٨)، ومن طريقه الضياء في المختارة (٩/٨٧).

8122 — ‘Abdullah ibn Busr al-Mazini said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah and said: “Whom do you count as martyrs from my ummah?” He said this three times. We said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah said: “If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permits me, I will inform him who the martyrs of his ummah are.” He said: “Then inform me: who are the martyrs of my ummah?” He said: “Support me.” So they supported him, and he said: “Whoever believes in Allah, strives in the path of Allah, and fights until he is killed is a martyr.” He said: “Then the martyrs of my ummah would be few. The one killed in the path of Allah is a martyr; the one who dies of a stomach illness is a martyr; the one who dies of plague is a martyr; the one who drowns is a martyr; and the postpartum woman is a martyr.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1508), and through him by al-Diya’ in al-Mukhtarah (9/87).
